source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Constitution at Work, Ch. 3 (Election and Representation).

sections.heading: 1. Elections and Democracy
points: **Elections** are essential to representative democracy — people choose their representatives periodically.
India follows **universal adult franchise** (every citizen 18+ can vote) and **secret ballot**.
Elections must be **free and fair**.

sections.heading: 2. Electoral Systems
points: **First-Past-The-Post (FPTP)** — India's system for Lok Sabha/Assemblies: the candidate with the **most votes** in a constituency wins (need not be a majority); simple, gives stable governments.
**Proportional Representation (PR)** — seats allotted in proportion to votes (used in some countries; in India for **Rajya Sabha and Presidential elections** via **Single Transferable Vote**).
FPTP favours a two-large-party system and local representation; PR reflects vote share more accurately.

sections.heading: 3. Reservation and Free/Fair Elections
points: **Reserved constituencies** for **SCs and STs** ensure their representation (based on population).
Free and fair elections require: **universal franchise, independent Election Commission, secret ballot, and an even playing field**.
There have been debates on **electoral reforms** (money power, criminalisation, need for state funding).

sections.heading: 4. Election Commission of India
points: The **Election Commission (Art 324)** is an **independent constitutional body** that superintends, directs and controls elections.
It is a **multi-member body** (Chief Election Commissioner + Election Commissioners).
Powers: prepare electoral rolls, conduct elections, enforce the **Model Code of Conduct**, register parties, allot symbols.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: India = universal adult franchise (18+), secret ballot.
Lok Sabha/Assemblies = First-Past-The-Post (FPTP); most votes wins.
Rajya Sabha/President = Proportional Representation (Single Transferable Vote).
Reserved constituencies for SCs and STs.
Election Commission = independent constitutional body (Art 324), multi-member.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Lok Sabha uses FPTP**; **Rajya Sabha and President use Proportional Representation (STV)**.
In **FPTP the winner needs the most votes, NOT a majority**.
The **Election Commission is a multi-member constitutional body (Art 324)**.
Reserved constituencies exist for **SCs and STs** (not OBCs at this level).
